goal: Decide if a router's proposal joins the app. A stale, unclear or clashing proposal never becomes part of it.

app.name: proposal-admission
app.title: Proposal admission
app.purpose: Decide whether a router's proposal is admitted, refused, or returned with an open issue, from whether its intent and registry revision are current, whether it is ambiguous, whether its constraints are resolved and how many selected features conflict.

fields.name: revision
fields.means: whether the intent and registry revision match the expected ones

fields.name: ambiguity
fields.means: whether the proposal lists an unresolved ambiguity

fields.name: constraints
fields.means: whether the proposal lists an unresolved constraint

fields.name: conflicts
fields.means: selected features that conflict with another

meanings.admit: the selected features join the composition
meanings.refuse: refused: stale, or the composition is rejected
meanings.open: refused with an unresolved issue, ambiguity or constraint, to resolve and propose again

rules.why: app/src/ProposalAdmission.lex.tex admitProposal: staleIntent and staleRegistry are checked first (staleIntentRefused, staleRegistryRefused)
admitProposal: any ambiguity is unresolvedAmbiguity, never a default (ambiguityRefused)
admitProposal: an unresolved constraint is unresolvedConstraint (constraintRefused)
app/src/FeatureComposition.lex.tex hasConflict: admitComposition rejects conflicting features (compositionRejected)

app.otherwiseWhy: current, unambiguous, resolved and consistent: admitProposal returns the features

properties.why: a proposal against an old registry or intent is never admitted

stakeholders.name: App builder
stakeholders.text: Describes an app in plain words and needs only current, unambiguous, consistent parts to reach it.

stakeholders.name: Registry maintainer
stakeholders.text: Publishes versioned feature contracts and needs a proposal made against an older registry revision to be refused.

components.name: Router
components.text: The model that reads the description and proposes versioned feature references with a confidence; inference belongs to the runner, not the kernel.

components.name: Feature registry
components.text: The registry of canonical versioned feature contracts that admission resolves references against.

threats.name: Confidence as permission
threats.text: A router's high confidence is taken as a grant, budget or evidence for a proposal.

control.name: Confidence grants nothing
control.text: Admission never reads confidence to decide, and the kernel proves confidence cannot grant a permission or raise a budget.

threats.name: Stale registry
threats.text: A proposal written against an older registry revision is admitted with contracts that changed.

control.name: Revision match proved
control.text: A stale proposal is never admitted, proved for every request.

threats.name: Router-authored contract
threats.text: A router supplies its own contract text in place of the registered one.
threats.accepted: Admission resolves canonical contracts from the supplied registry by key and version and never accepts router-authored contracts (proposalBoundary); the app sees only the outcome of that resolution.

quality.text: Every ambiguous or unresolved proposal is answered open, so the builder resolves it.
quality.measureText: Requests with an ambiguity or unresolved constraint answered admit.
